Sean / Kim — forwarding Starlite’s procurement questions (see below). Need quick guidance on allowable discount bands and a supply-risk construct we can offer without exposing us to open-ended GPU market volatility. High-level asks: 

- Starlite is asking whether we can offer price protection (cap) vs pass-through. My recommendation: offer a two-way corridor for GPU price movement with a trigger band (+/- X%) and a cap for increases (e.g., pass-through above 15% increase, with Redwood sharing first 7%). That preserves predictable economics for them while limiting Redwood exposure.
- Discount bands: I propose we can approve up to 10% off list for a 12-month $250k+ commit; up to 16% for a 24-month commit but that needs executive sign-off.
- Credit for SLA/availability: we should offer a standardized credit schedule (hours of downtime -> % credit) and for supply outages add an escrowed credit as they requested; legal to review escrow mechanics.

Attaching a draft clause for the GPU supply-risk language (gpu_supply_clause_draft.docx) and an updated estimate (starlite_updated_estimate_v2.xlsx) with a column showing the proposed discount bands. 

Can you confirm: 1) internal approval to offer a 10% discount on 12-month >=$250k deals (self-approve), and 2) sign-off path for the supply-risk clause (legal needed + your final approval).

Thanks —
Vanessa

Vanessa — thanks for the write-up. I’m comfortable with the approach below with two guardrails:

1) Discount guardrail: frontline ops (AE) may approve up to 10% on a 12-month commit >= $250k ARR equivalent. Anything beyond 10% routes to me for commercial approval. For 24-month we require written exec approval above 12%.

2) Supply-risk clause: we should avoid unconditional pass-through. Approve a structured protection: 
   - Pricing indexation trigger: if a validated market index for GPU compute increases > 15% over a rolling 90-day window, Redwood may invoke a cap-and-share: Redwood absorbs first 7% of increase, customer absorbs next 8%, anything beyond 15% becomes subject to renegotiation.
   - For short-term supply disruptions (unavailable reserved capacity beyond agreed SLA), offer an escrowed credit pool (pre-funded by Redwood for first incident) and a reconciliation process tied to capacity shortfall hours. Legal to draft exact wording; product ops to confirm feasibility of the escrow mechanics.

Kimberly — please confirm finance is comfortable with the 7% absorption band and the escrow approach on deals of this size. If finance signs off, Vanessa can communicate the structure to Starlite and include the GPU supply clause draft.

—Sean

Marta / Tom — thanks for the patience. Per internal guidance here’s a concise proposal we can take to PO/contract: 

1) Commercial summary (quick):
- Commitment: 12 months reserved pool (80 A100-equivalent baseline + 2.5x burst), monthly commitment billing.
- Pricing: baseline list in workbook; committed discount: 10% off list for commitments >= $250k ARR-equivalent.

2) Supply-risk protection (short form):
- Indexation & cap: if validated GPU index increases >15% over a 90-day rolling window, Redwood will absorb the first 7% of the increase; Starlite will absorb the next 8%; increases beyond 15% trigger a negotiation clause (no immediate pass-through).
- Escrowed credit for capacity shortfall: Redwood will seed an incident credit pool for the first major capacity outage event; subsequent events will follow a reconciliation schedule tied to documented shortfall hours. Legal to finalize escrow mechanics.
